handback.t:
The full research pipeline beats plain routing on delivered quality in every treatment world. Most of that gain is the reuse path plus retrieval, and the generator->critic pass adds nothing net of cost. `cargo test --release --offline --lib` passes (197 passed, 0 failed, including 6 new research tests). The board block is appended to `results/research_board.md`.

**What I built**
- **`src/research.rs`:**
  - `ResearchSession::run_task` runs retrieve (Knowledge over `hash_embed`, passing the best verified note as Context), route (default `CoupledBrain` = warm(hebbian-robust) + health benching; guarded(hebr) is an opt-in via config), and draft.
  - The critic is the verified SecondOpinion/HierSecondOpinion gate; a flag triggers a retry by the best other agent.
  - Graded outcomes are recorded `delay` tasks later through `feedback_delayed` (the coupling reuse path), the gate's calibration and `Knowledge::credit`.
  - `ResearchConfig` is `#[serde(default)]` and everything is off by default.
  - Fetching goes through the `ApprovedSources` allow-list (from config), with `NoFetch` as the default and `FixtureFetcher` for tests. `session.ingest()` turns fetched docs into notes. No network code anywhere.
- **Tests:** off == bare `CoupledBrain` decision-by-decision, NoFetch returns Disabled, allow-list blocks an unapproved source and adds nothing, plus three more.
- **`src/lib.rs`:** I appended only `pub mod research;`. `coupling`, `knowledge` and `addons` are still present; `pub mod defaults;` was not there yet.
- **`src/bin/e3_research.rs`:** 7 synthetic worlds and 10 arms (plain, plain-g, full, full-g, three ablations, three single parts). Pipeline knobs are tuned on seeds 1-8, evaluated on held-out 31-60, and confirmed on frozen 61-90. Each run does 336 paired t-tests with Holm. Two runs are identical except runtime.

**Results (gross quality at 2000 tasks, full vs plain, 31-60 | 61-90)**

Every treatment world is a Holm WIN on both sets:

| World | full vs plain, 31-60 | 61-90 |
|---|---|---|
| halluc-recur | +0.156 [.140,.172] | +0.170 |
| low-error | +0.114 | +0.107 |
| diluted-embedding | +0.179 | +0.170 |
| lazy-checkers | +0.185 | +0.170 |
| recur-only | +0.107 | +0.120 |
| irrelevant-notes | +0.118 | +0.101 |

- **Control (identical agents):** gross quality ties exactly. Net of extra calls it is a small Holm loss of -0.003 on both sets, from the critic's checking cost.
- **Where the gain comes from:** reuse alone (graded outcomes into the router) gives about +0.10 over plain. This is the earlier x3 weak-feedback result re-derived, because plain only ever sees the near-constant hook bit. Retrieval adds +0.015 to +0.058 on top of reuse, and +0.000 in irrelevant-notes. That gain exists because I built a quality gain from notes into the world.
- **Critic, negative:** full vs -crit is not significant in every world on gross quality. Net of cost it is -0.004 to -0.034, mostly Holm losses.
- **Critic cost:** it spends 0.16 to 1.1 extra agent calls per task depending on the world (0.09 in the control); retrieval and reuse add zero. The best operating point is retrieval + reuse with no critic.
- **Critic on a weak router:** it raises gross quality (+0.005 to +0.053) but rarely nets positive after cost.
- **guarded(hebr) front:** full-g also beats plain-g everywhere, but warm does at least as well in every world. It is not a better default here.

**Caveats** (the board block lists the full set)
- The world is fully synthetic.
- The critic's retry replaces the draft; an oracle variant that delivers the better of the two was not run and would favour the critic.
- Mid-session I fixed two issues:
  - a mislabelled "no-recurrence" world, now renamed diluted-embedding, with a real irrelevant-notes world added;
  - a warm_k confound, so every arm without the reuse path now uses its own tuned warm_k.
